name: Hydrafacial

lead: Hydrafacial is a branded multi-step facial that leaves skin looking fresher, brighter and smoother straight after the session, with little downtime. It cleanses, exfoliates, clears pores with suction and finishes with serums.

A handheld tip delivers a water-based solution and exfoliating agents while applying suction, removing dead surface cells and debris. It is a type of hydradermabrasion, itself classed as a variant of microdermabrasion. The effect is superficial rather than deep remodelling. Published research is a few small studies, including a 20-person open-label acne study and an imaging study of skin changes.

paras: Aestheticians or clinicians perform it in clinics and spas. People use it as a maintenance treatment, often before events or on a regular schedule, since the glow and smoother texture are temporary and sessions are repeated. Costs vary by clinic.
Microdermabrasion-type procedures are described as having few side effects, with temporary dryness, sun sensitivity or rare bruising reported. Results are temporary.

angle.text: Hydrafacial cleanses, exfoliates, extracts and applies serums, giving a fresher, brighter, smoother look right after treatment with little downtime. Removing dead skin and debris is what produces the immediate glow. The published evidence base is a few small studies.

lead: Hydrafacial is a branded facial treatment that combines cleansing, chemical exfoliation, suction-based extraction and serum application using a single handheld device. It is commonly described as a form of hydradermabrasion, which encyclopedias class as a type of microdermabrasion using water-based sprays and a textured tip [1].

It is offered in aesthetic clinics and spas and is discussed online as a maintenance treatment for a short-term glow and smoother skin. Published studies are few: an imaging study using line-field confocal optical coherence tomography examined microscopic skin changes [2], and an open-label trial in mild-to-moderate acne enrolled 20 adults [3].

paras: The treatment is delivered in stages: cleansing and peeling, suction-based extraction, and infusion of serums. The acne study describes a three-step process of this kind [3]. Hydradermabrasion is classed as a type of microdermabrasion, a non-invasive exfoliation that removes the outermost dead cells and is typically repeated every few weeks [1].

A 2024 study used line-field confocal optical coherence tomography, a non-invasive imaging method, to visualise microscopic anatomical changes after hydradermabrasion. Its authors note that clinical studies validating the procedure with objective histological assessment have been scarce [2].
A 12-week multicenter open-label study enrolled 20 adults with mild-to-moderate acne who were to receive six Clarifying Treatments, one every two weeks [3].

Registered trials include a phase 4 study of three treatments on skin quality, hydration and barrier in 27 adults [4], and scalp studies of the Keravive variant in androgenetic alopecia (44 participants) [5] and self-perceived hair thinning (15 participants, not yet recruiting) [6].

Microdermabrasion in general is described as having few side effects, with temporary dryness, sun sensitivity or, rarely, bruising and scratches reported. Crystal-based systems carry additional risks such as eye injury, which do not apply to water-based designs [1].

Hydrafacial appears in skincare discussions as a convenient pre-event or maintenance treatment. Because results are temporary, it is usually discussed alongside, not as a replacement for, daily skincare and medical acne treatment.
